title: Finance Cockpit
tagline: The AI build, and the rates and credit paying for it

tiles.label: US 10-Year Treasury
tiles.note: The anchor rate — discounting everything else on this board, including the cash flows the AI build is being valued on.

tiles.label: Real 10-Year Yield
tiles.note: The 10-year yield less headline CPI inflation — what a Treasury buyer earns after inflation, on today's yield and the last published price level. Only as current as the CPI print it leans on.

tiles.label: Nvidia
tiles.note: The pure-play on AI capex: almost every dollar of hyperscaler datacentre spend passes through it.

tiles.label: Semiconductors
tiles.note: VanEck Semiconductor ETF — the AI supply chain in one instrument.

tiles.label: Semis vs S&P 500
tiles.note: Semiconductors priced in units of the S&P. A ratio, not an index — nothing is normalised or weighted, so the only thing it can move on is the AI trade leading or lagging the broad market.

tiles.label: High-Yield Credit Spread
tiles.note: ICE BofA US high-yield option-adjusted spread. Not AI-specific — no free public series is — but the datacentre build is increasingly debt-funded, and this is the price of that debt for the weakest borrowers. It widens before capex plans get cut.

tiles.label: Investment-Grade Spread
tiles.note: ICE BofA US corporate option-adjusted spread — where the hyperscalers themselves borrow. Also not AI-specific.

tiles.label: Nvidia Revenue (TTM)
tiles.note: Trailing twelve months, summed from the quarters Nvidia has actually filed. The demand side of the AI trade: this is the revenue the capex turns into.

tiles.label: Hyperscaler Capex (TTM)
tiles.note: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta combined, trailing twelve months, from their cash flow statements. The spending itself — the number the whole question turns on.

tiles.label: Hyperscaler Cash Flow (TTM)
tiles.note: The same four companies' cash from operations. What the capex is being funded out of, before it has to be funded with debt.

tiles.label: Capex ÷ Cash Flow
tiles.note: The share of the hyperscalers' operating cash flow going into property and equipment. The closest thing here to a single bubble gauge: below roughly half is a business reinvesting, and a number climbing toward and past 100% is a build being financed by something other than the cash the business throws off. Both legs come from the filings, so it moves four times a year, not daily.

tiles.label: US CPI (year on year)
tiles.note: Headline CPI for all urban consumers, not seasonally adjusted, against the same month a year earlier — the way the inflation rate is quoted. BLS publishes it mid-month for the month before.

tiles.label: Japan FX Reserves
tiles.note: Japan's official reserve assets excluding gold, reported monthly by the Ministry of Finance and carried by the IMF. Falls when the MoF sells dollars to defend the yen.
